title: Arrangers and singers for his bands
summary: Don Redman wrote for Pearl Bailey, others for Vinson; ballads went to a white arranger; later a country blues guitarist sang.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Yeah. That's something I didn't ask you about. Who was writing for you during these years?
Oh, I had many writers.

Well, I mean like with the first band, with the big band in the beginning. What kind of writers did you pick on, in the very beginning, when you started rehearsing? Did you -- Buster Harding or people like that?
No.
Who, then? Can you remember?
Well, I had three vocalists in the band.
Yeah.
And all three of them was different.
Yeah.
And I had three different writers.
Yeah.
Don Redman used to do things for Pearl Bailey.
Oh, did he?
And Don Kirkpatrick --
Oh, yeah.
-- used to do things for Eddie Vinson. He did all of Eddie Vinson's things.
Oh, yeah.
And the ballad things, I used to have a white boy do all the ballads.
What was his name? Can you remember?
I can't remember off hand who he was.
Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. I see.
And then some of the swing things, I would get different swing arrangers.
Yeah.
To do the --
Yeah. People that you knew, and people that you --
Yeah.
-- that would come in and ask you if they could do things for you, too, I guess.
Yeah.
Yeah. Well, then, when you had the seven pieces, did you write some of the things?
No. Not all of them, but some of them.
Yeah.
But the majority of all the things, I would get an arranger, and have him to come and listen. Before he would make arrangements for me, he would have to come and listen, to see what I was doing.
Yeah.
Before he would make arrangements.
To see what you wanted.
Yeah.
Yeah.
Before he could make arrangements for me.
In that time, Cootie, who was doing any vocals for you then? With the seven pieces.
Oh, we had a guitar player. What was his name? And a blues singer, too. He played the guitar. I'll think of his name after awhile.
All right. Funny, I'm not sure. You don't know who he worked with --
Larry Pale.
Oh, I see. Was he a good guitar player?
Yeah. He was a country guitar player.
Oh.
Played that country guitar and sang country blues.
